_comment: Every variable the website reads. `name` must match .env.example (checked), unless `notInExample` gives the reason it is deliberately absent. readBy: Node.

precedence.intro: The settings are read in this order. The first one that has a value wins.

steps.title: The real environment
steps.text: A variable set in the terminal (export NAME=value) or by the host. It always wins over the file, so a deployment can override .env without editing it.

steps.title: The env file
steps.text: The file named by TERUCON_ENV_FILE, otherwise .env next to package.json. It is re-read whenever it changes: save it and reload the page. Only HOST and PORT need a restart.

steps.title: The built-in default
steps.text: What the column below shows. A blank value in the file counts as not set.

precedence.envFileNote: The way to point the website at a different file (a relative path is relative to the project folder). Every test sets it, together with an explicit environment, so no test can ever read your real .env.

groups.title: Where the website listens
groups.blurb: Read by Express. HOST and PORT need a restart.

groups.title: The Design Studio's cold start
groups.blurb: Read by Express. Takes effect on the next request (no restart).

groups.title: Keeping the open studio safe
groups.blurb: Read by Express. STUDIO_REQUIRE_PASSCODE and TRUST_PROXY need a restart; the limits take effect on the next request.

groups.title: Analytics (PostHog)
groups.blurb: Read by Express and asked for by every page (GET /api/analytics). Takes effect on the next request.

groups.title: Sign-in and accounts
groups.blurb: Read by Express on every request, so a saved change applies at once (AUTH_REQUIRED and AUTH_STORE are read when the server starts). Rate limits and the other adjustable rules are NOT here: they are in the database, managed through the admin API (GET /api/auth/admin/settings).

groups.title: CRM (Zoho)
groups.blurb: A finished sign-up is queued and sent to Zoho CRM by a background loop. With these blank nothing is lost: the queue waits and is delivered once they are filled in.

groups.title: Inspiration import
groups.blurb: Read by Express on every request, so a saved change applies at once. Needs gallery-dl for the sites that use it (python/requirements.txt); picture links and web pages work without.

groups.title: Catalogue (Finder and catalogue admin)
groups.blurb: Read by Express on every request, so a saved change applies at once; from the root .env, not swatchroom/.env. With none of them set the catalogue is off. The Python side (the Modal app) has its own settings in three Modal secrets: docs/CATALOGUE_SETUP.md.

groups.title: TeruBot (the assistant on every page)
groups.blurb: Read by Express on every request, so a saved change applies at once. TeruBot talks to Gemini through the Design Studio's own Google key (GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, VERTEX_LOCATION): without a usable key it answers "AI is off" and nothing else breaks.

groups.title: Capture from a phone
groups.blurb: Read by Express on every request, so a saved change applies at once (CAPTURE_STORE is read when the server starts). The links the QR code and WhatsApp carry are built from CAPTURE_PUBLIC_URL, never from the Host header of a request. The WhatsApp Business settings are optional: without them the link is sent through the requester's own WhatsApp (wa.me) and there is no WhatsApp alert when a photo arrives.

vars.name: HOST
vars.effect: Where Express listens. 127.0.0.1 means only this computer. 0.0.0.0 exposes the server to the network: use it only on a trusted network.

vars.name: PORT
vars.effect: The port Express listens on. If it is taken, the server says so and exits.

vars.name: ALLOWED_HOSTS
vars.effect: Extra host names the site may be opened under (comma separated), for when it is served from a domain. Any other Host header is refused with 421.

vars.name: TERUCON_ENV_FILE
vars.effect: Path of the env file. Relative paths are relative to the project folder. Tests always set it.
vars.notInExample: it chooses the file, so it cannot live inside it; set it in the real environment

vars.name: LANDING
vars.effect: Which landing page the address "/" shows. new: the new landing page, built in memory from site/landing/ when the server starts and served pre-compressed with a strong ETag, its files under /lp/ for a year. classic: the earlier landing page (the site map's "home" page, pages/home.html). Set in .env, it is read again when the file changes: saving it is enough, no restart. Set in the real environment (Render's dashboard) it is read when the server starts, so the service has to restart. Anything but "classic" counts as new.

vars.name: STUDIO_WARMUP
vars.effect: The Design Studio's GPU services scale to zero and take 10-45 s to wake. With on, the landing page and the studio page ask the website to start them as soon as they open (POST /api/studio/warmup), so they are usually ready by the first scan; a started service is billed until it has been idle for a few minutes, even if the visitor never uploads a photo. With off the studio wakes them only when a photo is scanned.

vars.name: STUDIO_PREVIEW_OVERLAY
vars.effect: on: the Design Studio's instant preview (the 3D draw of a finish on the photo) is served from improved copies of 8 of the studio's own files in site/overlays/studio/ (lighting, soft edges, 8x anisotropic filtering, a level-camera guess for the estimate, seam repair), ahead of the studio's files of the same names; swatchroom/ is not edited. off: the studio's own files are served, to compare or to roll back. Read on every request; a browser shows the other version on its next load. Blank or unreadable means on.

vars.name: STUDIO_REQUIRE_PASSCODE
vars.effect: off: the website switches the studio's own STUDIO_PASSCODE (swatchroom/.env) off before the studio reads its settings, and puts server/lib/studioShield.js in front of it. on: the studio asks for its passcode as it does on its own, and the shield is not used. Read when the server starts.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_AI
vars.effect: Gemini calls (/api/ai) one browser may start per hour. This is the starting value: a limit the admin saves in the admin API (settings studio.limit.*) wins.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_VISION
vars.effect: Photo scans (/api/vision) one browser may start per hour. This is the starting value: a limit the admin saves in the admin API (settings studio.limit.*) wins.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_PIPELINE
vars.effect: Room analyses and wake-ups (/api/pipeline) one browser may start per hour. This is the starting value: a limit the admin saves in the admin API (settings studio.limit.*) wins.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_CHECK
vars.effect: Settings > Check runs (/api/check) one browser may start per hour. This is the starting value: a limit the admin saves in the admin API (settings studio.limit.*) wins.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_ROOMS
vars.effect: Room and room-file saves and deletes (/api/rooms) one browser may do per hour. Autosave is frequent, so this is the highest. This is the starting value: a limit the admin saves in the admin API (settings studio.limit.*) wins.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_ADDRESS_FACTOR
vars.effect: One network address may do this many times a browser's limit (a shared address: an office, a phone network), which also stops a visitor who clears cookies to get a new allowance. This is the starting value: a limit the admin saves in the admin API (settings studio.limit.*) wins.

vars.name: TRUST_PROXY
vars.effect: How many proxies sit in front of the site (Render: 1, set in render.yaml), or the proxy addresses. Without it the site sees the proxy's address for every visitor and cannot tell HTTPS from HTTP. Read when the server starts.

vars.name: POSTHOG_KEY
vars.effect: PostHog project key (phc_...), public by PostHog's design. Blank: the studio's own key in swatchroom/.env is used. Neither set: no analytics.

vars.name: POSTHOG_HOST
vars.effect: The API host PostHog gave the project; must be https. A malformed host switches analytics off.

vars.name: POSTHOG_REPLAY
vars.effect: Session replay, with all text and fields masked and photos blocked. It also needs replay switched on in the PostHog project itself.

vars.name: POSTHOG_ON_LOCALHOST
vars.effect: Off: nothing is sent while the site is opened as localhost, so test clicks do not fill the real project. on: send from this computer too.

vars.name: AUTH_REQUIRED
vars.effect: on: every page but the landing page, and the studio's costly API, need a signed-in account. off: development only, everything is open (the banner says so).

vars.name: AUTH_SECRET
vars.effect: 32+ random characters. Keys the one-time codes (they are stored only as an HMAC of this). Without it nobody can sign in, except on this computer in development, where a temporary one is made. Changing it invalidates codes in flight, not sessions.

vars.name: AUTH_ADMIN_TOKEN
vars.effect: 32+ random characters. The bearer token for the sign-in admin API (rate limits and settings, the security log, the CRM queue). Not set: that API does not exist (404). Never stored in the database.

vars.name: AUTH_STORE
vars.effect: Where accounts are kept. auto: the studio's MongoDB when the studio is mounted, else memory (lost at restart). memory or mongo to force one.

vars.name: AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE
vars.effect: auto: the sign-in cookie is Secure (and named __Host-terucon_session) on HTTPS requests. on or off to force it. Behind Render set TRUST_PROXY=1 so HTTPS is recognised.

vars.name: AUTH_EMAIL_PROVIDER
vars.effect: How code e-mails are sent. smtp (any SMTP service), console (development only: prints the code in the server window), off, or blank = auto: the console on a computer that only this computer can reach and NODE_ENV is not production (so `npm start` works while you try the site), nothing anywhere else. The console is refused on a server reachable from the network.

vars.name: AUTH_EMAIL_FROM
vars.effect: The sender, plain ASCII: Terucon <no-reply@your-domain>. Use an address on a domain you have set up with your mail service.

vars.name: AUTH_SMTP_HOST
vars.effect: The SMTP server, e.g. smtp.zoho.in.

vars.name: AUTH_SMTP_PORT
vars.effect: 465 (encrypted from the start) or 587 (STARTTLS).

vars.name: AUTH_SMTP_SECURE
vars.effect: tls (465), starttls (587) or none (this computer only). Certificates are always checked.

vars.name: AUTH_SMTP_USER
vars.effect: The SMTP login.

vars.name: AUTH_SMTP_PASS
vars.effect: The SMTP password (an app password where the service has them).

vars.name: AUTH_SMS_PROVIDER
vars.effect: How code text messages are sent. twilio, webhook (your own URL, for MSG91 or any gateway), console (development only), off, or blank = auto (as for e-mail).

vars.name: AUTH_SMS_TEMPLATE
vars.default: {code} is your Terucon verification code. It works for {minutes} minutes. Do not share it with anyone.
vars.effect: The text of the message. Must contain {code}; {minutes} is optional. For India the text usually has to match one registered with the operator.

vars.name: AUTH_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID
vars.effect: Twilio account SID (AC...).

vars.name: AUTH_TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
vars.effect: Twilio auth token.

vars.name: AUTH_TWILIO_FROM
vars.effect: The Twilio number to send from, +14155550100 style. Or use the messaging service below.

vars.name: AUTH_TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID
vars.effect: A Twilio Messaging Service SID (MG...), instead of a number.

vars.name: AUTH_SMS_WEBHOOK_URL
vars.effect: For AUTH_SMS_PROVIDER=webhook: an https:// URL that receives {to, message, code, purpose, minutes} as JSON for each text message and hands it to your gateway.

vars.name: AUTH_SMS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN
vars.effect: Sent as Authorization: Bearer to that URL.

vars.name: AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
vars.effect: Your Google OAuth client id (123-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com). Not secret. Turns on Google One Tap and the Google button. Add this site's address under "Authorised JavaScript origins" in Google Cloud.

vars.name: AUTH_CRM
vars.effect: zoho: new sign-ups are queued for Zoho CRM (delivered when the credentials below exist). off: nothing is queued.

vars.name: ZOHO_DC
vars.effect: Your Zoho data centre: in (India), com, eu, com.au, jp, ca, com.cn. Or set ZOHO_ACCOUNTS_URL.

vars.name: ZOHO_ACCOUNTS_URL
vars.effect: A Zoho accounts address for a data centre not in the list above, e.g. https://accounts.zoho.sa. Must be a Zoho address: the secrets are sent to it.

vars.name: ZOHO_CLIENT_ID
vars.effect: The Zoho API client id (api-console.zoho.in).

vars.name: ZOHO_CLIENT_SECRET
vars.effect: The Zoho API client secret.

vars.name: ZOHO_REFRESH_TOKEN
vars.effect: A Zoho refresh token with scope ZohoCRM.modules.ALL (or Leads/Contacts CREATE and WRITE), made with a Self Client.

vars.name: INSPIRATION_IMPORT
vars.effect: Switch the import on or off. Off: every inspiration route answers that importing is switched off.

vars.name: INSPIRATION_LIMIT
vars.effect: The most pictures taken from a board, album or project (1 to 100).

vars.name: INSPIRATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
vars.effect: How long to wait for gallery-dl before giving up (10 to 180).

vars.name: INSPIRATION_MAX_FILE_MB
vars.effect: The biggest picture file taken, in megabytes (1 to 50). More than 64 million pixels is refused whatever the size.

vars.name: IMPORTER_PYTHON
vars.effect: The Python that runs gallery-dl. Left out: the project's own python/.venv.

vars.name: IMPORTER_SCRIPT
vars.effect: The script that asks gallery-dl for the pictures of an address.

vars.name: CATALOGUE
vars.effect: Switch the catalogue on or off. Off: /finder and the search routes say it is not switched on; the shop keeps its colour demo.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_MODAL_SEARCH_URL
vars.effect: The address of the GPU search app on Modal (what modal deploy modal_app.py prints). https only. Blank: search is not set up.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_MODAL_INGEST_URL
vars.effect: The address of the ingest app on Modal. https only. Blank: the admin screen cannot start processing.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_MODAL_KEY
vars.effect: One of the API_KEYS of the Modal secret terucon-catalogue-keys. Sent to the two Modal addresses only, never logged or repeated to a visitor.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_MODAL_PROXY_KEY
vars.effect: Modal proxy-auth key; used only with CATALOGUE_MODAL_PROXY_SECRET, and only if the app was deployed with CATALOGUE_REQUIRE_PROXY_AUTH=1.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_MODAL_PROXY_SECRET
vars.effect: Modal proxy-auth secret; goes with CATALOGUE_MODAL_PROXY_KEY (neither is sent until both are set).

vars.name: CATALOGUE_MODAL_TIMEOUT_MS
vars.effect: How long to wait for Modal before saying it is waking up (200 to 300000 ms). A cold start takes tens of seconds.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_GCS_BUCKET
vars.effect: The Google Cloud bucket that holds the catalogue's pictures and releases. The same as in the Modal secret terucon-catalogue-gcp.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_GCS_PREFIX
vars.effect: The folder inside the bucket. The same as in the Modal secret. No leading slash and no .. part.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_GCS_KEY_JSON
vars.effect: The JSON key of the website's signing account, used only to sign picture and upload links, given as text so no file is kept on the server: the whole downloaded file between single quotes (not double), or the same file as base64. On Render, paste it as the variable's value. Wins over CATALOGUE_GCS_KEY_FILE if both are set.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_GCS_KEY_FILE
vars.effect: Alternative to CATALOGUE_GCS_KEY_JSON: a path to the JSON key file of the website's signing account. A path, not the JSON; on Render a Secret File at /etc/secrets/<name>. Ignored if CATALOGUE_GCS_KEY_JSON is set.

vars.name: CATALOGUE_SEARCH_PROFILE
vars.effect: balanced (the default since 2026-11-05: DINOv2 + SigLIP + colour + a Vertex AI image embedding, which tells wood from stone), fast (without Vertex AI) or full (also a Gemini description of the photo, about 5 s more). An explicit value wins: a .env or Render value of fast keeps fast.

vars.name: TERUBOT
vars.effect: on / off. Off switches the assistant's AI off everywhere (the widget then says so); the rest of the site is unaffected.

vars.name: TERUBOT_MODEL
vars.effect: A Gemini model id to use instead of the default (the studio's text model chain, first entry). Letters, digits and . _ - only.

vars.name: TERUBOT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS
vars.effect: The most Gemini may write per answer (128 to 4096).

vars.name: TERUBOT_HISTORY_LIMIT
vars.effect: How many of the latest chat messages are sent to Gemini (2 to 20).

vars.name: TERUBOT_TOOL_ROUNDS
vars.effect: How many times the assistant may look something up before it must answer (1 to 6).

vars.name: TERUBOT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
vars.effect: The whole reply, including every Gemini call and look-up, is stopped after this long (1 to 120).

vars.name: TERUBOT_LIMIT_ACCOUNT
vars.effect: Messages one signed-in account may send per hour.

vars.name: TERUBOT_LIMIT_ADDRESS
vars.effect: Messages one network address may send per hour, signed in or not.

vars.name: TERUBOT_LIMIT_ANONYMOUS
vars.effect: Messages one network address may send per hour while NOT signed in (the landing page is public).

vars.name: TERUBOT_VOICE
vars.effect: The speaker of the spoken answers in a live conversation: a Google Chirp 3 HD voice name (the same one speaks Indian English and Hindi), or off to use the browser's own voice. Needs the Cloud Text-to-Speech API enabled in the Google project of the key; billed by Google per character.

vars.name: CAPTURE
vars.effect: on or off. Off: the launcher disappears and every capture route answers 503 capture-off.

vars.name: CAPTURE_STORE
vars.effect: auto (the studio's MongoDB when the studio is mounted, else memory), mongo, or memory. Memory is for a computer with no database: photos are lost at every restart. Read when the server starts.

vars.name: CAPTURE_PUBLIC_URL
vars.effect: The address a phone opens, for example https://terucon.example (https only; http only for this computer or a private address; no path). Left out, RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL is used. On this computer the page's own address is used and the panel warns that a phone cannot open it. Never taken from a request's Host header anywhere else.

vars.name: CAPTURE_SESSION_MINUTES
vars.effect: How long a link works (5 to 1440).

vars.name: CAPTURE_MAX_PHOTOS
vars.effect: Photos one link takes (1 to 100).

vars.name: CAPTURE_MAX_PHOTO_MB
vars.effect: The biggest photo the server takes, in MB (1 to 10). The phone page shrinks a photo to about 1 MB first. A photo is kept in MongoDB as text, so 10 MB is the most a 16 MB document allows.

vars.name: CAPTURE_KEEP_DAYS
vars.effect: Days a photo and its link are kept before the database deletes them (1 to 365). The requester can delete sooner; deleting an account deletes its photos.

vars.name: CAPTURE_DEFAULT_COUNTRY_CODE
vars.effect: Added to a WhatsApp or phone number typed without a country code.

vars.name: CAPTURE_LIMIT_SESSIONS
vars.effect: New links per account per hour.

vars.name: CAPTURE_LIMIT_UPLOADS
vars.effect: Photos per network address per hour (a phone network shares addresses, so it is generous).

vars.name: CAPTURE_LIMIT_WHATSAPP
vars.effect: WhatsApp messages the server sends per account per hour. 0 turns server sending off (the wa.me message is used).

vars.name: WHATSAPP_TOKEN
vars.effect: The WhatsApp Business Cloud API access token (Meta). Secret: kept in a property that is never printed, logged or sent. Not set: see CAPTURE_PUBLIC_URL's note above.

vars.name: WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID
vars.effect: The business phone number's id from Meta's dashboard (digits).

vars.name: WHATSAPP_API_VERSION
vars.effect: The Graph API version in the request address. Meta's examples differ; check the dashboard.

vars.name: WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_PHOTO
vars.effect: The approved template that tells the requester a photo arrived. Three variables: who, how many, which page. Without it there are no WhatsApp alerts.

vars.name: WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_LINK
vars.effect: The approved template that sends the link to a number. Three variables: from, link, minutes. Without it the panel opens the requester's own WhatsApp with the message ready.

vars.name: WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_LANG
vars.effect: The templates' language code, for example en or en_US.
